answer: A coastal observatory stays honest when every new identity must chart a distinct star no other identity has claimed, recording it in a shared atlas at dawn while a distinct astronomer checks the sighting against a live signal from the sky. The first fake sweeps one sky sector, the tenth sweeps ten, the twentieth sweeps twenty, because claimed stars never return to the pool. Bulk farming fails since one sextant scans a single sector at a time and needs recalibration between sightings, so a thousand fakes would need a thousand dawns, like one net catching one fish per cast.
